laws.rule: Gran Paradiso National Park (it spans the Aosta Valley and the Piedmont side): camping and bivouac with a tent are prohibited outside equipped areas; one-night emergency mountaineering bivouacs are allowed where no hut serves the place or the hut is full. Open fires are prohibited across the whole park, and camp stoves and barbecues are allowed only in equipped areas where authorised. Parking campers or any vehicle used as lodging is prohibited except in equipped areas. Driving off road, including on mountain paths, is prohibited. Leaving rubbish, even temporarily, is prohibited. The text says it holds until the park plan and regulation are approved; the park's own site (pngp.it) was not reachable on 6 November 2026, so check that nothing has replaced it.
laws.heading: Parco Nazionale Gran Paradiso, regolamento-stralcio (version of 31 March 2003)

laws.rule: In the same park, dogs are prohibited, except working sheepdogs, guard dogs on private ground, rescue dogs, and dogs on a lead in the valley-floor areas and, in summer, on trails the park signs (the appendix lists these for 15 July to 31 August, for example the Valnontey to Rifugio Sella trail). Picking or taking wild plants is prohibited; so is taking mushrooms, truffles, mosses and juniper berries. Strawberries, raspberries and blueberries may be eaten on the spot but not carried off. Taking rocks, minerals, fossils or archaeological finds is prohibited. Administrative fines run from EUR 25.82 to EUR 1,032.92 (about A$41 to A$1,641; RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293); some breaches, such as picking ten named rare plant species or lighting a fire, are criminal under law 394/1991.
